summary: Nora now keeps a history of everything she changes in her own records, so her state at any past moment can be restored for testing.
details: Every change to her in-place records (messages, notes, reminders, standing, culture, media descriptions, loop state and caches) is kept as a dated version; nothing she reads changes, and a pruned or expired row is kept in that history rather than lost.
Each doctrine and Dreamer instruction load, each config file and each process start is recorded, so which instructions and settings were in force at a moment can be answered.
nora snapshot --at T reports what every store held at T and what was in force then, and with --into copies it into an empty sandbox database; without --into it writes nothing.
limitations: History starts at this upgrade: earlier states are reconstructed only as far as each record's own dates allow, and rows deleted before it are gone.
Memory (Honcho), the presence summaries (until step 2) and events (until step 2b) cannot be restored as of a past moment; the snapshot says so.
The upgrade writes one history row per existing row of the covered tables, once, at the first start after deploy.
Eval cases still seed through the per-room snapshot; moving them onto the whole-store snapshot is a later change.
